conventions.convention: Complex inner products are linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second.
F(H) is the bosonic symmetric Hilbert direct sum; the degree-zero sector is C, the vacuum is (1,0,...), and particle-number indices start at zero.
Creation is linear in its mode vector; contraction and annihilation are conjugate-linear in that vector. The core commutator is [S_-(f),S_+(g)]ψ = ⟨g,f⟩ψ.
Canonical permutations act on zero-based slots. On one-based tensor positions the action uses π̂(k)=1+π(k−1), with inverse permutation in the tensor action.
The Fourier transform uses exp(−2πiX·ξ). The fixed-N kinetic symbol is Σ_i ħ²|ξ_i|²/(2m_i), so its differential realization is −Σ_i ħ²Δ_i/(8π²m_i).
Finite entropy sums omit zero eigenvalues; the infinite weight example explicitly assigns zero contribution to a zero weight. Logarithms are natural.

The transverse free energy is ε(k)=α|k| with α>0; Π(0)=0 is irrelevant to Lebesgue classes. Sector energy domains are maximal multiplication domains, followed by squared-energy summability across sectors.
Cutoff vectors satisfy support in 0<ε≤Λ and g/√ε∈h. The field sum is restricted to D(H_f); the atomic dimension is at least one.
Dyson products have the latest vertex on the left. C=2Σ_j||D_j||||g_j||/ħ excludes η₀, which appears once as |η₀| in the bounds.

K_t is defined only for t>0 and has mass 2π/ħ. Emission coefficients use c_j=⟨D_jv_a,v_b⟩ and M=Σ_jc_jg_j. The density-limit assertion excludes Δ=Λ and concerns the explicit first-order coefficient, not exact long-time evolution.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, the specified square-summable symmetric-sector direct sum F(H) is a Hilbert space with dense finite-particle space and isometric coordinate embeddings. Given self-adjoint T_n on every sector, including the vacuum sector, their direct sum is self-adjoint on the stated coordinate-domain and squared-image-summability domain.

Under Countable Choice and Choice, on a σ-finite measure space with μ(X)>0, a real measurable finite-a.e. multiplier M_m is self-adjoint on its stated maximal domain. Its regular spectral PVM is E(B)=M_{1_{m^{-1}(B)}}, and its spectrum is the stated essential range of m.

Under Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice, the specified transverse space is closed and separable, its energy multiplier and symmetric-sector energy multipliers are positive self-adjoint, and H_f is positive self-adjoint on the stated direct-sum domain. For every β>0, e^{-βH_f} is not compact and hence not trace class.

Under Countable Choice, A_+(f)=closure(S_+(f))=S_-(f)* and A_-(f)=S_+(f)*=closure(S_-(f)) on the displayed maximal sector domains. They are closed, densely defined mutual adjoints; the weighted domain D₁ is contained in both domains and carries the stated bounds and norm identity.

For the stated cutoff vectors and d≥1 Hermitian atomic matrices, the field sum on D(H_f) is symmetric with H_f-bound zero. H_a⊗I+I⊗H_f+η₀Σ_jD_j⊗φ(g_j) is self-adjoint on C^d⊗D(H_f) and bounded below for every real η₀.

For the stated cutoff model and vacuum initial vector, ||Ψ_n(t)||≤(|η₀|Ct)^n/√(n!). The Dyson series converges uniformly on compact nonnegative time intervals in the H_f graph norm, solves the interaction-picture equation, and satisfies e^{-itH₀/ħ}Ψ(t)=e^{-itH/ħ}Ψ₀, with the stated truncation tail.
For a supplied complete orthonormal family (e_j) indexed by the positive integers, ε_j>0 and β>0, D_β is trace class exactly when Σ_je^{-βε_j}<∞; in that case its trace is Π_j(1−e^{-βε_j})^{-1}.
For ω>0 and β>0, G_βe_n=e^{-βωn}e_n is positive trace class with trace 1/(1−e^{-βω}); its normalized density has number expectation 1/(e^{βω}−1), and all stated polynomial moments are finite.

For N≥1, positive masses and ħ, the stated Fourier kinetic operator is positive self-adjoint with domain W^{2,2}. Adding a real bounded measurable potential preserves self-adjointness on that domain, gives lower bound −||V||∞, and preserves the C_c^∞ core; the finite-component extension has the stated properties.

For the stated finite-N real Coulomb sum, each distance multiplier has kinetic relative bound zero. H=K+M_V is self-adjoint and bounded below on W^{2,2}, with C_c^∞ as a core; the finite-component extension has the stated properties, and equal masses with permutation-invariant coefficients give self-adjoint symmetric and antisymmetric restrictions.

Slater vectors of orthonormal orbitals have norm one and equal √(n!) times the antisymmetric projection. For the stated orthogonal normalized spatial orbitals, bounded real even pair kernels give expectations D±X with real absolutely convergent integrals. For repulsive Coulomb kernels and W^{1,2} orbitals, the states lie in the multiplier domain and D≥0, X≥0.

For a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension d≥1, self-adjoint H and β>0, the stated Gibbs density attains −β^{-1}log Z for the functional tr(ρH)−β^{-1}s(ρ), which is a lower bound for every density. Entropy is at most log d, with equality exactly at d^{-1}I.

K_t has mass 2π/ħ and, for J∈L¹ with a representative continuous at Δ, ∫K_t(x)J(Δ+x)dx tends to (2π/ħ)J(Δ). Under the stated emission data and density hypotheses, the explicit coefficient divided by t tends to 2πη₀²J_b(Δ)/ħ for 0<Δ<Λ and to zero for Δ>Λ; Δ=Λ is excluded.

concerns.concern: The Statement permits H={0}, but the Facts & Assumptions Given block adds H≠{0}. The coordinate proof works for H={0} as well, where F(H)=C and all positive-degree projections vanish; the proof setup should retain the Statement's scope.

Proof steps 1.1 and 3.2 contain justification tags before subsequent displayed formulas and continuation paragraphs belonging to the same step. This violates the required complete-step paragraph and trailing-tag layout. The algebraic argument itself is sound.

F2 refers to 'the stronger choice hypotheses of the general direct-sum theorem', and step 1.1 refers to its 'Axiom of Choice premise'. The current cited Hilbert direct-sum construction assumes only Countable Choice, including clause (f). These descriptions are stale. Step 1.1 also contains an internal tag group followed by further argument.

Step 1.1 places '[F1, F7, algebra]' before the continuation beginning 'For a Borel set B', then supplies another tag group at the end. The complete step needs a single trailing justification group under the prescribed layout.

Steps 1.1 and 3.1 have internal tag groups before displayed formulas and subsequent continuation text; step 3.1 also splits its complete argument into multiple paragraphs. These are proof-layout defects, independent of the valid reducing-subspace and sector-domain arguments.

The title 'Bounded fixed-N operator' suggests boundedness of the operator, whereas the Statement concerns an unbounded kinetic operator with a bounded potential. Already V=0 gives an unbounded Fourier multiplier. The title should identify the bounded-potential hypothesis.

Clause (d) and proof 1.4 apply the origin-centered Hardy supplier to a translated Sobolev function without explicitly deriving preservation of its weak gradient. The required short argument is the change of variables in the weak-derivative test identity for v(x+·). The inverse-square multiplier-domain estimate is now present in the Statement, so this is a local justification omission rather than a missing domain conclusion.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.2 says the map (u,v)↦⟨u,u₀⟩⟨v,v₀⟩ 'is C-linear on H×K'. It is bilinear, not linear on the product vector space: taking H=K=C and u₀=v₀=1 gives uv, which sends (1,0)+(0,1) to 1 although both summands map to zero. The subsequent descent uses the correct bilinear tensor relations, so the wording can be corrected locally without changing the theorem.

seams_checked.note: Declared prerequisite context; the dynamics arguments use exact domain-preserving Stone evolution and locally prove the graph-valued Dyson construction. No bounded-Dyson theorem is applied to the unbounded field interaction.

Tensor completion, permutation projections, Euclidean product identification, scalar multiplier self-adjointness and density laws are used at their stated scope. Finite-component and reducing-subspace extensions are proved locally. The supplier wording alert does not alter its tensor conclusion.
The diagonal adjoint/core lemma is applied after supplying a complete countable orthonormal family; the multiset index set is explicitly enumerated before the trace construction.

The three-dimensional Hardy bound is used with W^{1,2} hypotheses, then extended to global slices by smooth approximation and Fatou. The translated weak-derivative justification is recorded as a reader-closeable concern.
Repeated-orbital exclusion uses the actual antisymmetric tensor-square projection, rather than identifying it with the symmetric Fock sector.
The mean-position counterexample uses the multiplier spectral law at m(x)=x on nonzero Lebesgue L²(R).

Spectral support is stated as probability-one concentration, and position/momentum uses are nonzero Euclidean multiplier specializations. Generic Facts wording omits μ(X)>0, but the actual applications satisfy it.
Multiplier PVMs are used on nonzero Euclidean spaces; finite internal components are handled componentwise. Actual uses meet the scalar supplier hypotheses.
Unitary spectral transport and energy-law conclusions use the exact support and probability-one concentration statements.
Ground-state position and momentum densities use multiplier PVMs and transport through the 2π-normalized Fourier transform with momentum multiplier 2πħξ.
The free-flow multiplier representation uses the scalar spectral measure componentwise on Euclidean L²; its bounded functional-calculus specialization preserves the momentum normalization.
This is declared page prerequisite context. Its current item bodies do not directly cite batch-41 items; their sector and occupation constructions use the composite permutation suppliers.

The Coulomb example preserves normalized orthogonal W^{1,2} orbitals, positive coupling and multiplier-domain conclusions. Strict positivity of exchange for nonzero overlap is supplied by an additional local Gaussian/approximate-identity argument.
The variational consumer explicitly identifies its semibounded form domain with D(|H|^{1/2}) before applying the ground-gap overlap estimate.

Finite Gibbs, Slater and product criteria retain their hypotheses. Coulomb realization explicitly substitutes mathematical masses m/(4π²) to match the declared −ħ²Δ/(2m), adds bounded external terms separately, and proves the spin-component reduction.
Dilute identities and product convergence are obtained through the corresponding physical theorem and scalar supplier; the chemical-potential condition is preserved.

Fock number domains, transverse energy domains and non-trace-class Gibbs conclusions are preserved. Fixed-mode embeddings distinguish normalizable packets from free-energy eigenmodes and distinguish second moments from literal squared-operator domains.

Geometric weights are transferred with a separately declared effective energy. Gibbs compression is distinguished from an invariant mode or normalized full-continuum Gibbs state; no thermalization is inferred.

Positive-dimensional cutoff self-adjointness is applied with d≥1 and zero dimension is handled directly. Dyson constants include the coupling once, amplitude coefficients use the linear-first convention, and the golden-rule consumer retains density continuity and the excluded cutoff boundary. Arbitrary-coefficient photon-law arguments use only the scalar kernel clauses and prove their measure claims locally.
